title: Endless reel of deformable GL sheets
summary: Virtual offset in items on a modulo-wrapped belt (`mod(i − offset + N/2, N) − N/2`, the first work follows the last going forward), wheel-burst detector (≥ 40 px after a 30 ms gap, 500 ms cooldown, doubled and released at `1 − (1 − .22)^frames`), snap after 200 ms idle, segmented sheets twisted and folded by one `uBend` = velocity · `sin(π·p)` that is exactly 0 at rest, canvas-drawn card art, horizontal belt on landscape and vertical stack on portrait; a button index with `aria-current` and a live "n / 8" counter; flat sheets and one step per input under reduced motion, plain list in the static tier
variants: Three.js segmented planes with a pixel-unit camera and canvas-drawn card art (this, default)
Horizontal belt on landscape, vertical stack of full-width cards on portrait (same engine, uVertical swizzle)
OGL: Plane({ widthSegments: 48, heightSegments: 24 }) + Program with the same vertex shader
Real project screenshots: KTX2 textures in place of the canvas art, one per work, the button list unchanged
